title: Greetings
description: Say hello, goodbye and thank you like a local.

grammar_note.title: Politeness levels
grammar_note.body: Japanese greetings change with formality. ありがとう (arigatou) is casual; ありがとうございます (arigatou gozaimasu) is polite. With strangers, teachers, or at work, always prefer the longer polite forms. おはよう → おはようございます works the same way.

culture_note: Bowing (おじぎ) accompanies most greetings in Japan. A small nod works between friends; a deeper bow (about 30°) shows respect to elders, customers, or teachers. Handshakes are rare — when in doubt, bow!

vocab.example_ja: こんにちは、たなかさん。
せんせい、おはようございます。
こんばんは、おげんきですか。
さようなら、また あした。

study_guide.heading: Greetings change with the clock
study_guide.body: おはようございます (morning), こんにちは (daytime), こんばんは (evening). The polite morning greeting keeps ございます; dropping it (おはよう) is casual, for friends.

study_guide.heading: Politeness is built in
study_guide.body: ありがとう becomes ありがとうございます when polite. すみません means both 'excuse me' and 'sorry' — one of the most useful words in Japanese.

study_guide.heading: Meeting someone new
study_guide.body: はじめまして = nice to meet you (literally 'for the first time'). Follow with your name + です and どうぞ よろしく.
